notes: Every racial ability in the client: SkillLineAbility rows on the nine skill lines whose name contains “Racial”. The client names them inconsistently — some “Dwarven Racial”, some “Racial - Gnome” — so they are normalised to the race here.
Skyborne is not a classic race. It carries five abilities of its own (Walk on Air, Skysight, Read Ley Line, Elemental Insight, Wind Blessed) and appears only in this build.

The weapon-specialisation racials are flat passives, not procs. Human Sword Specialization (#20597) is aura 290 MOD_CRIT_PCT at 2%, gated by SpellEquippedItems on weapon subclasses 7 and 8 (sword and two-handed sword), and has no SpellAuraOptions row at all — so no proc mask, no chance, no charges. The same holds for Orc Axe Specialization, Dwarf Mace Specialization and Night Elf's Elune's Light. Their text says “all spells and attacks”, and the general crit aura matches that rather than the narrower MOD_WEAPON_CRIT_PERCENT or MOD_SPELL_CRIT_CHANCE.
The racials that genuinely do proc carry a real mask, and the tooltip shows it: Gnome Eureka! at ProcTypeMask 87376 and 100%, Undead Touch of the Grave at 69972 with 5% and 10% variants.
A few racials are restricted to certain classes by the row's own class mask; those are marked on the ability.
Descriptions are resolved by the repo's own tools/tooltip parser via tools/foreverdesc, the same as the class pages.
No hotfixes are applied. The beta client's DBCache.bin is for build 61916, not 69876, so the overlay matched nothing.

Where an ability procs, the tooltip expands SpellAuraOptions.ProcTypeMask bit by bit against the repo's own PROC_FLAG enum, and states outright whether a periodic tick can trigger it — that needs bit 18 DEAL_HARMFUL_PERIODIC or bit 21 DEAL_HELPFUL_PERIODIC. Where there is no SpellAuraOptions row at all the tooltip says so, because that means a flat passive rather than something that triggers. The column is a two-word array and both words are read; the client also stores 0x80000000, which reads as a negative in SQLite and is not named in the enum, so it renders as bit 31 rather than being guessed at — it appears on break-on-damage crowd control such as Frost Nova, Entangling Roots and Chains of Ice.

The proc table distinguishes the three separate periodic bits, because they differ by direction: bit 18 DEAL_HARMFUL_PERIODIC and bit 21 DEAL_HELPFUL_PERIODIC are your own ticks, while bit 19 TAKE_HARMFUL_PERIODIC is a periodic ticking on you. In this build 18 and 21 are set on no ability at all, and 19 on 54 — so a tooltip that said only “periodic” would misread the one case that actually occurs.

Where a spell carries one of the spell attributes the sim names in tools/database/dbc/enums.go, the tooltip lists it — CAN_PROC_FROM_PROCS (21 abilities) and CANT_CRIT (17). A proc that lacks CAN_PROC_FROM_PROCS says so explicitly, since whether an effect can be set off by another proc is not visible in its text: Gnome Eureka! has the flag, Undead Touch of the Grave does not. The client carries 16 attribute words and the repo names flags in only four of them, so nothing beyond those four is guessed at.

A proc's rate limits are shown alongside its chance: SpellAuraOptions.ProcCategoryRecovery is the internal cooldown (292 spells in the database have one; Undead Touch of the Grave is 1s), ProcCharges the number of uses, CumulativeAura the stack cap. Where there is no internal cooldown the tooltip says so, since that is the difference between a proc limited only by its chance and one that is rate-capped. SpellProcsPerMinuteID is set on no spell in this build, so no proc here uses the real-PPM system.
